plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders, where the winner pays the second-highest bid. This is equivalent to a Vickrey auction. In a Vickrey auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. This strategy maximizes profit regardless of what other bidders do. Therefore, I will bid my private value.

I need to maximize my profit. Since I pay the second-highest bid, I want to bid as high as possible to win, but not so high that my profit is negative. My value is $34. I will bid slightly above what I anticipate the other bidders might bid, while ensuring I still make a profit. Given the value range of $0-$49, and that other bidders are rational, they will likely bid below their value. I will bid slightly below my value to ensure a positive profit if I win, but high enough to be competitive.

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a twist: the winner pays the second-highest bid. This is a Vickrey auction variant. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding less risks losing to a bid lower than your value, while bidding more risks winning and paying more than necessary (though the payment rule mitigates this somewhat, it's still not optimal). Since all bidders are rational and know this, they will likely bid their true values. I will bid my true value to maximize my profit in the long run.
